evidence: Cic. Inv. 2.14: cēnātī discubuērunt ibīdem (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: In Plautus the second i is short, ibĭdem (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Caes. BG 1.4.2: omnēs clientēs … eōdem condūxit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of motion towards; with locī it can also mean “in the same place”: rēs eōdem est locī quō relīquistī (Cic. Att. 1.13.5).

sources: Lewis & Short: ibidem · Lewis & Short: eodem
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 360.
